where: i1-station-powermap-reciprocal: powermap sector readout (angText) with complex.js exactAngle

where: i1-station-powermap-reciprocal: js/stations/reciprocal.js:893 (buildLinks, `prose(a, s.title)`); same pattern in js/stations/powermap.js links; .station-link in css/components.css:471 is `display:inline-flex; gap:8px`
problem: [minor] Round-3 issue 4 is only fixed in the DOM, not on screen. `prose()` puts a text node, a `<sup>` and a second text node directly inside the flex anchor, so each becomes a separate flex item with an 8px gap, and `vertical-align: super` does not apply to flex items. In the screenshot (reviewB/crops/rc-link-zoom.png, desktop and phone) the link reads 'z  n  : Fans and Parabolas', with a small unraised n floating between gaps, not 'zⁿ:'. R9c passes anyway because it only counts one `<sup>` and no caret. I confirmed it by script: anchor display is flex, child nodes are '#text,SUP,#text', gap is 8px. The meaning is still guessable, so it is cosmetic.
fix: In `link()`, build the label as one element: `const t = mk('span'); prose(t, s.title); a.appendChild(t);`. Then the anchor has a single flex item and the sup renders raised. Add a visual assertion to R9c: the sup's bounding box top is above its parent span's text box, or the sup's previous sibling is inside the same span.

where: i1-station-mappings-cr: mappings w-plane near the origin (z about 0.3 + 0.4i, z = -1, any w near 0 with the Cartesian grid on); see /home/user/math-viz/docs/review/iter-1/i1-station-mappings-cr/reviewA/r2/m2-near0.png and m2-near0-label-crop.png
problem: [minor] Carried grid curves run straight through the address labels "Arg w = 2.287", "also 8.57", "r = 0.716" and "u = -0.47". At 1x a curve between "=" and "2" looks like a minus sign, so a Q2 Arg can read as negative. Legible at 2x, and the builder reported this crowding as known and left it unfixed. It is the plane's label placement over a dense grid, not a station bug, but it sits where students park z.
fix: Plane owner: give the address labels a --surface backing or halo strong enough to knock grid lines out. Or lower the carried-grid alpha near labels. Station-side stopgap: drop alpha from 0.85 to about 0.6 when s is 1 and w is within 1.5 units of 0.

where: i1-station-mappings-cr: cauchy-riemann u = c mode with a typed v that is huge but finite (for example exp(30*x) at x = 1.9, or x^20); also the build note 11.1 item 7 and design 2.5
problem: [minor] The builder dropped the "(off the scale)" key line, saying no chip can reach 1e6 units. That is true for the six chips, but typed v in u = c reaches it. |B| then prints through toFixed as "8.528580126914589e+25". The w-view clamps at 1e6 units, centred at (2, 1000000) while f(z0) = 2 + 5.7e24 i, so f(z0) is off the plane and the picture is empty. No note says so, and the design's "view always contains f(z0)" fails here. Very exotic input.
fix: Format fixed3 with toExponential(3) above 1e6, and when the view hits the 1e6 clamp (or f(z0) is outside it) add one sentence to #cauchy-riemann-wcap (for example "off the scale"). Update design 2.5 so it no longer says unreachable.

where: i1-station-mappings-cr: #cauchy-riemann-v-error text (parser message reuse, design C-2 / ARCHITECTURE 10.4.7)
problem: [minor] An empty v shows "Type a formula in z, for example z^2 + i z." in a v(x, y) field that rejects i. A real-looking sqrt(x) is rejected with "Remove the i" although the student typed no i. Both messages are as designed, but they can confuse.
fix: Special-case the empty string with an own message (for example "Type a real formula in x and y, such as x + y."). Reword MSG_REAL to "... at every point (it is the imaginary part of f), for example sqrt(x) is not real for x < 0." Keep U-C5 in step.

where: i1-station-mappings-cr: #cauchy-riemann-polar-note on /#problem-3-2-1 (text comes from js/data/problems.js, 3.2.1 routes.polar)
